pr_title: Allow to skip HashWithIndifferentAccess value conversion
pr_body:
Fix: https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/54433

And use it to avoid casting hash values in ActiveModel::Dirty.

This is a tentative fix, I'm not particularly happy with it, but I can't think of any better solution. @matthewd what do you think?
pr_comments: Huh, `store_accessor` actually relies on the fact that `Hash` gets converted to `HashWithIndifferentAccess`

> Huh, `store_accessor` actually relies on the fact that `Hash` gets converted to `HashWithIndifferentAccess`

Indeed, that can be fixed though.
Alright, the issue was actually limited to JSON columns, but I fixed it.

> The `store_accessor_for` calls feel like extra indirection at first glance

Well, that indirection is already used by `read_store_attribute` and `write_store_attribute`, the fact that the change related methods weren't using it was a bug IMO, it just happened to work thanks to another bug.

> be split between the "`send` to get store" and "read/write store contents". But that's probably complication for another day.

I mostly fear the overhead of calling lots of small methods. What's unfortunate is that if the type of the attribute is known at class definition time, we could simply generate all that code, but in some cases (e.g. `json`) we need to access the database schema, so...
Alright, I think it's good to go, but not too sure about backporting this. @matthewd any opinions?

Yeah, I'm split on backporting. On one hand, someone could be [accidentally] depending on the current HWIA-conversion behaviour; on the other hand, it's only `changes`, so quite a narrow path to end up depending on it... and it _is_ data mangling.

Is this a recent regression, or a longstanding edge case?
I haven't double checked, but that's probaly been there for over a decade.

issue_context.title: ActiveRecord::Dirty#changes alters type of hash values
issue_context.body:
Because `ActiveModel::AttributeMutationTracker` uses a `ActiveSupport::HashWithIndifferentAccess` to store changes (see https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/4d42d34adda4011e770c18136966cb5df08c9220/activemodel/lib/active_model/attribute_mutation_tracker.rb#L26-L32), it inadvertently changes the type of hash values from `Hash` to `ActiveSupport::HashWithIndifferentAccess`.

This caused bugs in production for us, because we use `acts_as_list` which has this bit of code: https://github.com/brendon/acts_as_list/blob/02fe238ab4cdfe66fb93994526ef3c3ff1f7fc2f/lib/acts_as_list/active_record/acts/list.rb#L442-L452, which essentially reverts the changes using the stored dirty changes to perform some checks, and then re-applies the changes.

This can become a problem when used with a serialized column which uses YAML, as by default `ActiveSupport::HashWithIndifferentAccess` cannot be serialized (see `test_acts_as_list_raise` below).

### Steps to reproduce

```ruby
begin
  require "bundler/inline"
rescue LoadError => e
  $stderr.puts "Bundler version 1.10 or later is required. Please update your Bundler"
  raise e
end

gemfile(true) do
  source "https://rubygems.org"
  gem "activerecord", "~> 8.0.0"
  gem "sqlite3"
  gem "acts_as_list"
end

require "active_record"
require "minitest/autorun"
require "logger"

# This connection will do for database-independent bug reports.
ActiveRecord::Base.establish_connection(adapter: "sqlite3", database: ":memory:")
ActiveRecord::Base.logger = Logger.new(STDOUT)

ActiveRecord::Schema.define do
  create_table :posts, force: true do |t|
  end

  create_table :comments, force: true do |t|
    t.integer :post_id
    t.integer :position
    t.text :metadata
  end
end

class Post < ActiveRecord::Base
  has_many :comments, inverse_of: :post
end

class Comment < ActiveRecord::Base
  belongs_to :post, inverse_of: :comments

  serialize :metadata, type: Hash

  acts_as_list scope: [:post_id]
end

class BugTest < Minitest::Test
  def test_change_class
    post = Post.create!
    comment = Comment.create!(post: post)
    comment.metadata = { foo: "bar" }

    assert_equal Hash, comment.changes["metadata"][0].class
  end

  def test_acts_as_list_raise
    post = Post.create!
    post2 = Post.create!

    comment1 = Comment.create!(post: post)
    comment2 = Comment.create!(post: post)

    comment2.metadata = { foo: "bar" }
    comment2.post_id = post2.id
    comment2.save # this raises when metadata is changed

    assert_equal comment2.post, post2
    assert_equal comment2.position, 1
  end
end
```

### Expected behavior

Probably that `post.changes` returns the original Hash-object instead of converting it to a `ActiveSupport::HashWithIndifferentAccess`.

I realize this could also be considered a bug in `acts_as_list`, but the fact that this occurs in such a widely used gem seems to indicate that this behavior is at least surprising. It also doesn't look like this conversion happens on purpose, and is just a coincidence with how `ActiveSupport::HashWithIndifferentAccess` performs merges of other Hashes.

### Actual behavior

`Hash` is converted to `ActiveSupport::HashWithIndifferentAccess`.

### System configuration
**Rails version**: 8.0.1
**Ruby version**: 3.2.3
comments: Urk, this is bad, and won't be easy to fix. `HashWithIndifferentAccess` has no API at all to allow inserting a regular Hash without casting it...

Tentative fix here: https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/54437

This doesn't only apply to `act_as_list`, any model having a `serialize` attribute that contains hashes is impacted too.

review_comments:
I'm tempted to claim that the documentation might be clearer if we just add the kwarg to `[]=` and keep the alias, even though it'll only be usable (with standard syntax) via the alias.

(On the other hand, maybe we don't want to document the option at all for now...)

I think we probably should offer that option. I'd rather not add it to `[]=` as I suspect it's a hotspot.

The first version of this PR exposed a new `raw_store` method rather than a keyword arg. Not sure which is better.

But either way, offering a way to skip that conversion make sense to me.
Unrelated, but maybe change the `send` ☝🏻 to `public_send` while we're nearby?
Done, and I refactored all this a bit further.
